doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: No major-label contract: gender and management
summary: Liston says being a woman explains it, and she never had a manager except Colby, which may have been good.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Before we go to the music, I wanted to ask you, does it strike you funny, with all your experiences and your writing, technique, and expertise in doing so many – on your horn and everything – does it strike you funny or kind of sad that a large record company has never signed you to a contract? Do you think it’s because of the gender or something?
I’m a woman. That’s that. I don’t know. I don’t have a manager that pushes me out there and all of that.
That is one of the problems.
But maybe it was good, because I wouldn’t – I don’t know if I was ready for that.
